scope: Independent cross-check of the new or changed TeX-audit interfaces only; no source files changed.
conclusion: No mandatory correction found in the inspected interfaces. Original domain restrictions are retained; validity and convergence are conclusions rather than new caller hypotheses.

checks: All odd characters, including imprimitive ones, are summed; no GRH or weight condition has been introduced.
The factor 2/varphi(N), complex conjugation of chi(m), and plus-equal/minus-opposite congruence signs exactly match TeX.
The if Nat.Coprime(n*m)N branch is exactly the source coprimality indicator, including n=0 or m=0; nonunit character values vanish.
Even N and N>=4 match the paper's actual Goldbach modulus domain. NeZero N is a redundant typeclass witness on that domain, not a stronger arithmetic assumption.
Source kernel is (X^v-x^v)/(v^2 log x) with x=sqrt X; the implemented kernel has exactly those factors.
X>1 ensures x>1 and log x nonzero. In the application X=N/2 this follows from the existing modulus range.
The numerator's first derivative at zero is log X-log sqrt X=log sqrt X, so the residue is +1, not a derivative term or an extra factor 2.
MeromorphicOn together with punctured limit v*K(v)->1 expresses the simple-pole residue without mistaking the totalized value at v=0 for a meromorphic point value.
TeX explicitly interprets ell=0 as the identity; poissonAction 0 f=f implements this for every f.
The scalar Poisson kernel at ell=0 is not a Dirac mass and should not be used in an ordinary convolution to implement that identity.

For ell>0 the theorem gives Integrable, pointwise nonnegativity and integral exactly 1. The convolution equality for arbitrary f is only its definition, not an assertion that all arbitrary-f convolutions are integrable.
No analytic assertion is made for ell<0. Applicability to the logarithmic-derivative boundary data remains part of proving the existing Lemma 6.4, whose proof is intentionally sorry.
The orientation realConvolution(f,g)(t)=integral f(u)g(t-u) agrees with the source P1*Pell calculation.
For ell>0 the product integrand is integrable: the second kernel is bounded and the first is integrable. Integrability appears as a conclusion.
P1*Pell=P(1+ell) and P(1+ell)(t)<=(1+ell)P1(t) have the correct normalization and comparison direction.

The restriction ell>0 is necessary for the ordinary scalar-kernel convolution; ell=0 is already represented by the separate identity action. No case in the paper's nonnegative parameter range is lost.
Fixed c>0, even N>=4, N>exp(10c), and GRH(N) are precisely the source hypotheses.
These imply 0<alpha(N,c)<1/10<sigmaStar=1/9<beta=1/8. Thus ha:alpha(N,c)<beta is mathematically implied and the existing Riesz choice at sigmaStar belongs to the same strip.
Every HardySpace, residualOperator and boundaryTraces occurrence uses exactly alpha(N,c), beta and the same ha; no accidental mixing with alpha(N,1) occurs.

Both boundary lines and all four kernel L2 combinations are retained. Kernel representation, spectral-data nonemptiness and the two action-integral Integrable statements are conclusions, not stronger caller premises.
The theorem does not claim a c-uniform bound or threshold: it states validity for each source-admissible realization. This preserves fixed-c versus varying-c quantifier distinctions.

The newly added orthogonality, Perron, Poisson and A.1 validity statements are exact identities or existence/regularity statements; they introduce no Big-O constant with a changed quantifier dependency.
The original Lemma6.4 absolute constant remains quantified before N and sigma. A.1's fixed-c norm asymptotic remains separate, with constants allowed to depend on phi and c.
All new theorem proofs remain by sorry. This cross-check does not certify mathematical proofs or resolve the previously registered implementation choices.
